venues.name: Rosewood Mayakoba
venues.note: Lagoon suites reached by boat, a Sense spa on its own island, and a hush that has held Forbes Five-Star status for years, the coast's most complete grand resort.

venues.name: Maroma, A Belmond Hotel, Riviera Maya
venues.note: Belmond's beach house on one of the Caribbean's most beautiful strands, whitewashed, thatched, deeply private, recently and beautifully restored.

venues.name: Chablé Maroma
venues.note: Freestanding jungle-and-beach villas, a spa built around a cenote, and a kitchen led by Mexico City's Jorge Vallejo, wellness and gastronomy in one hush.

venues.name: NIZUC Resort & Spa
venues.note: A discreet, design-led enclave on its own peninsula minutes from the airport, Forbes Five-Star, with a celebrated ESPA spa and quiet, contemporary calm.

venues.name: Banyan Tree Mayakoba
venues.note: Asian-inflected pool villas threaded through mangrove and lagoon, Banyan Tree's signature spa ritual transplanted to the Caribbean, now a Forbes Five-Star house.

venues.name: Etéreo, Auberge Resorts Collection
venues.note: A serene Auberge house raised on stilts through the mangrove to a white-sand beach, spare, elemental design and a quietly excellent kitchen.

venues.name: Waldorf Astoria Cancun
venues.note: A sleek, compact Waldorf on a fine stretch of Cancún beach, 173 rooms, a Maya-inspired spa and the assured service of the flag.

venues.name: Fairmont Mayakoba
venues.note: The largest of the Mayakoba houses, 401 rooms across 45 acres of jungle and lagoon, with a strong spa and a genuinely family-minded run.

venues.name: Hotel Esencia
venues.area: Xpu-Ha (between Playa del Carmen and Tulum)
venues.note: A former duchess's beachfront estate turned intimate hideaway, the only Three-Key hotel on this coast, and its most personal luxury.
credentials: MICHELIN Three Keys (2025), the coast's only Three-Key hotel

venues.name: Chablé (Casa Chablé), Tulum
venues.note: An off-grid, solar-run beach camp inside the Sian Ka'an reserve, a handful of tented villas, wellness-led and utterly removed.

venues.name: Le Chique
venues.note: Jonatán Gómez Luna's deconstructed, theatrical Mexican tasting menu, trained through elBulli, Noma and El Celler de Can Roca, and the most ambitious kitchen on the coast.
credentials: MICHELIN Guide Mexico 2025 Mentor Chef Award

venues.name: HA'
venues.note: Carlos Gaytán, the first Mexican chef to hold a Michelin star, cooks a water-themed nine-course journey through his native flavours in a jewel-box room.

venues.name: Cocina de Autor Riviera Maya
venues.note: Nahúm Velasco's nine-course tasting menu inside Grand Velas, the coast's rare Michelin star within an all-inclusive resort, and holder of the 2025 Service Award.

venues.name: Arca
venues.note: Wood-fired, jungle-chic cooking on the Tulum beach road, open flame, local produce and one of the coast's most atmospheric rooms.

venues.name: Axiote Cocina de México
venues.note: Chef-driven Mexican street flavours with real technique, vivid, generous and honestly priced, a Bib Gourmand favourite off Playa's Fifth Avenue.

venues.name: Cetli
venues.note: A tiny, home-style kitchen reinterpreting Mexican classics with the season, mole and slow-cooked dishes done with real heart.

venues.name: Mestixa
venues.note: A bright, market-led kitchen crossing Mexican produce with Asian technique, inventive, good value and a critics' Bib pick.

venues.name: Punta Corcho
venues.note: Sea-facing, produce-driven cooking in the sleepy fishing town between Cancún and Playa, a considered Bib Gourmand kitchen away from the crowds.

venues.name: Frida
venues.note: Grand Velas' ode to Mexican haute cuisine, regional classics, mezcal and a formal, romantic room beside its Michelin-starred sibling.

venues.name: Casa del Lago
venues.note: Rosewood's lakeside room, Mexican by day, Italian by night, with the polish and produce of a Forbes Five-Star house.
credentials: At Rosewood Mayakoba, MICHELIN Two-Key, Forbes 5-Star hotel

venues.name: Zapote Kitchen
venues.note: The kitchen beside Rosewood's award-winning Zapote Bar, Maya-rooted, farm-to-table cooking matched to one of the region's great drinks lists.
credentials: At Rosewood Mayakoba, MICHELIN Two-Key, Forbes 5-Star hotel

venues.name: Hartwood
venues.note: The wood-fired, off-grid restaurant that shaped Tulum's whole dining scene, everything cooked over open flame, the menu set by the day's catch and market.
credentials: Long regarded as the restaurant that defined Tulum dining, a Caribbean-coast landmark

venues.name: Posada Margherita
venues.note: A barefoot, beachfront Italian of homemade pasta and just-caught fish, the romantic, candlelit heart of old Tulum.
credentials: A long-standing Tulum-beach institution, the town's most-loved Italian

venues.name: Fisher's
venues.note: Mexico's most respected modern seafood house, ceviches, tostadas and grilled catch done with real freshness and buzz.
credentials: An acclaimed Mexican seafood group, a benchmark for the coast

venues.name: Tulum Ruins (Zona Arqueológica)
venues.note: The only Maya city built on the sea, grey temples on a limestone cliff above a turquoise cove, El Castillo watching over the water. A photogenic, easy-walking site the whole family can do in a cool morning, then descend the wooden stairs to swim off the little beach below.

venues.name: Cobá & the Nohoch Mul Pyramid
venues.note: A vast, still-jungled Maya city where you pedal or take a bici-taxi between temples under the canopy. Nohoch Mul, one of the peninsula's tallest pyramids, reopened for climbing in December 2025 on a new wooden staircase, the reward at the top is an ocean of unbroken rainforest.

venues.name: Museo Maya de Cancún & the El Rey ruins
venues.note: The city's serious cultural stop, minutes from the beach resorts: a purpose-built museum of Maya artefacts paired with the small seaside El Rey ruins, where iguanas sun themselves on the platforms. An easy, air-conditioned culture fix for a day when nobody wants to travel far.

venues.name: MUSA, Museo Subacuático de Arte (underwater museum)
venues.area: Cancún / Isla Mujeres National Marine Park
venues.note: Over 500 life-size sculptures by Jason deCaires Taylor standing on the seabed, slowly turning into living reef. Snorkel the shallow Nizuc gallery, scuba the deeper Manchones one, or stay dry over a glass-bottom boat, a surreal outing that works for mixed-ability groups.

venues.name: Isla Mujeres & Punta Sur
venues.note: A slow, golf-cart island where Punta Sur, the easternmost point of Mexico, drops in sculpture-dotted cliffs to the Caribbean, with a small Maya shrine to Ixchel at the tip. Charter a private catamaran for the day and the family swims, lunches and watches the sunset without a crowd in sight.

venues.name: Playa Norte, Isla Mujeres
venues.note: Regularly named among the Caribbean's finest beaches, flour-soft white sand and water so shallow and calm you can wade out a long way, ideal for grandparents and small children alike. Claim a shaded bed at a beach club and let the afternoon dissolve.

venues.name: Gran Cenote, Tulum
venues.note: One of the most beautiful open-and-cavern cenotes, crystalline freshwater over pale rock, with turtles and small fish, and stalactite chambers you can snorkel into. A gentle, unforgettable introduction to the underworld the Maya held sacred.

venues.name: Dos Ojos Cenote system
venues.note: "Two Eyes", twin sapphire pools opening into one of the world's great flooded cave systems, superb for both easy snorkelling and world-class cavern diving. A private guide can tailor it from a splash for the children to a proper cave dive for the certified.

venues.name: Cenote Azul, Bacalar
venues.note: A vast, deep, startlingly blue open cenote on the shore of the Bacalar lagoon, ringed by jungle and a laid-back restaurant deck. The plunge into cool, clear water is a highlight of any Bacalar day.

venues.name: Ruta de los Cenotes, Puerto Morelos
venues.note: A jungle road strung with dozens of cenotes, open pools, cavern swims, zip-lines and rope swings, far less trafficked than the Tulum circuit. A private driver lets you pick two or three, from a serene swim for elders to an adventure stop for teenagers.

venues.name: Xcaret eco-archaeological park
venues.area: Riviera Maya near Playa del Carmen
venues.note: A polished, all-day park built around underground rivers, wildlife, and a genuinely spectacular evening show of Mexican music, dance and history. Multi-generational catnip, small children, teenagers and grandparents all find their own version of the day.

venues.name: Xel-Há natural aquarium
venues.note: A calm natural inlet where the freshwater river meets the sea, snorkelling among fish in glass-clear water, gentle floats and cliff jumps, with food and drink included. The most relaxed of the eco-parks, easy on non-swimmers and older travellers.

venues.name: Xplor adventure park
venues.area: Riviera Maya near Playa del Carmen
venues.note: The high-adrenaline sibling, long zip-line circuits, amphibious vehicles through the jungle, and swimming and rafting through stalactite-hung underground rivers. The park teenagers and thrill-seeking adults will remember longest.

venues.name: Playa del Carmen & Quinta Avenida
venues.note: The Riviera's stylish heart, a long pedestrian avenue of boutiques, mezcalerías and rooftop restaurants a block back from the sand. An easy evening of strolling, shopping and dinner, with the Cozumel ferry leaving from its pier.

venues.name: Puerto Morelos & the reef
venues.note: A small, unspoilt fishing town between Cancún and Playa, with a leaning lighthouse, good seafood and a protected national-park reef just offshore. The most authentic, low-key village base within easy reach of the airport.

venues.name: Akumal, swimming with sea turtles
venues.note: "Place of the Turtles", a sheltered bay where green sea turtles graze on seagrass in waist-deep water, snorkelled with a licensed guide. A wildlife encounter that reliably thrills children and adults, best booked early with a private guide to avoid the day-tripper rush.

venues.name: Sian Ka'an Biosphere Reserve
venues.note: "Where the sky is born", a million-plus acres of mangrove, lagoon and reef where you float the ancient Maya canals, spot dolphins, turtles and hundreds of birds. A private boat safari here is the wild, pristine counterpoint to the resort coast.
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Sian Ka'an

venues.name: Cancún Hotel Zone beaches & Nichupté Lagoon
venues.note: The famous 22-kilometre strip of white Caribbean sand backed by the calm Nichupté Lagoon on its inner side, swimming, catamaran sailing and sunset cruises without leaving the resort corridor. The effortless default for a day when the family just wants sea and sand.

venues.name: Private yacht or catamaran charter, Cancún–Isla Mujeres
venues.note: The signature UHNI day here, a crewed yacht to Isla Mujeres for swimming, snorkelling the reef and an anchored lunch, entirely on your own timetable. Add a chef and it becomes the trip's most memorable, most private afternoon.

venues.name: A temazcal ceremony
venues.note: The ancient Maya steam-lodge ritual, led by a shaman with herbs, chanting and darkness, a cleansing, ceremonial experience quite unlike a spa. A grounding, spiritual counterpoint to the beach, and one many Indian travellers find deeply resonant.

venues.name: Mezcal & tequila tasting
venues.note: A guided flight through Mexico's agave spirits, from crisp blanco tequilas to smoky artisanal mezcals, with a sommelier explaining terroir and craft. A sophisticated evening for the adults while the children are looked after at the resort.

venues.name: Luxury beach clubs of the Riviera Maya
venues.note: Design-led beach clubs, daybeds, ceviche, cocktails and a DJ over the turquoise water, from Tulum's boho-chic scene to Playa's polished spots. The stylish, low-effort way to spend a whole day on the sand in comfort.

venues.name: Río Secreto underground river
venues.area: Riviera Maya near Playa del Carmen
venues.note: A guided wade and float through a half-flooded cave of stalactites and mirror-still water, helmet-lamps lighting formations older than the Maya. A cool, awe-inspiring hour underground that even nervous swimmers can do in a life vest.

venues.name: Cozumel, El Cielo & Palancar snorkelling
venues.note: "Heaven", a shallow, sandy-bottomed sandbar where dozens of starfish rest in impossibly clear water, best reached by private boat from Cozumel. A gentle, magical snorkel that suits families and non-divers.

venues.name: Xcaret México Espectacular evening show
venues.area: Riviera Maya near Playa del Carmen
venues.note: A 300-strong cast telling the story of Mexico through pre-Hispanic ball games, charro horsemanship, regional dance and mariachi in a vast open-air theatre. The single most crowd-pleasing evening in the region for a multi-generational group.

venues.name: Tulum cliff-top beach & Playa Paraíso
venues.note: Beneath the ruins runs one of the Caribbean's most beautiful beaches, powder sand, palms and warm shallow water at Playa Paraíso. Combine an early ruins visit with a long swim below the temples for the classic Tulum morning.

venues.name: Kaan Luum lagoon
venues.note: A serene turquoise lagoon ringed by a darker central cenote plunging deep into the earth, far quieter than the beach. A calm, photogenic swim and float away from the crowds, easy to fold into a Tulum day.

venues.name: Deep-sea & fly fishing charters
venues.note: World-class waters, offshore for sailfish, marlin and mahi-mahi from Cancún, and the flats of Ascension Bay for bonefish, tarpon and permit. A private crewed charter tailors the day from trophy fishing to a gentle family reef troll.

venues.name: Kite-surfing & watersports at Puerto Morelos / Tulum
venues.note: Steady Caribbean trade winds make this coast excellent for kite-surfing, paddleboarding and sailing, with private instructors for beginners. An active morning for the sportier members of the group while others linger over breakfast.

venues.name: Cenote Dos Ojos to Cenote Nicte-Ha, Sac Actun
venues.note: The Sac Actun system is among the longest underwater cave networks on earth, and Nicte-Ha's lily-covered surface makes a serene, easy snorkel beside the more famous Dos Ojos. A quieter, lovelier pairing for those who want the cenotes without the crowds.

venues.name: Zapote Bar
venues.note: Rosewood Mayakoba's jungle-set cocktail bar, Maya-inspired, farm-to-glass drinks built on Mexican distillates, ranked for years among the continent's best.

venues.name: Bagatelle Tulum
venues.note: The Saint-Tropez French-Mediterranean import on Tulum beach, rosé, long lunches and a glossy, high-energy day-into-night scene.
credentials: Part of the international Bagatelle beach-club group, a Tulum-beach flagship

venues.name: Taboo Tulum
venues.note: Rosa Negra group's beach club, Mediterranean plates, sax-and-violin 'happenings' and Tulum's signature sundown party energy.
credentials: Grupo RosaNegra beach club, a Tulum-beach landmark

venues.name: Rosa Negra Beach
venues.note: Pan-Latin sharing plates, live percussion and sparkler-lit tables, the group's flagship beach club and one of Tulum's most-booked nights.
credentials: Grupo RosaNegra flagship, a defining Tulum beach club

venues.name: Coco Bongo
venues.note: Cancún's legendary mega-club, acrobats, tribute acts and non-stop spectacle, the definitive high-octane night in the Hotel Zone.
credentials: Cancún's best-known nightclub, a Hotel-Zone institution

venues.name: Casa del Agua bar
venues.note: The Waldorf Astoria's poised beachfront bar, considered cocktails and Caribbean views in one of Cancún's most refined new houses.
credentials: Inside the Waldorf Astoria Cancún, MICHELIN One-Key, Forbes 4-Star hotel
